title: The target users of the guideline are clearly defined.

chain_of_thought.step1_locate: Scanned 'GUIDELINE DEVELOPMENT AND REVIEW PROCESS' and 'Recommendations' sections for 'Users' or 'Intended Users' terms
step2_evidence: The 2017 VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG) for the Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Primary Care offers health care providers an evidence-based framework to evaluate, treat, and manage persons with type 2 diabetes mellitus in the context of their individual needs and preferences (8).
The CPG strongly encourages clinicians to incorporate shared decision making and partner with their patients.
chain_of_thought.step3_reasoning: The guideline uses vague terms 'health care providers' and 'clinicians' without specifying target roles (e.g., GPs, specialists, nurses). This meets the 'vaguely mentioned' criterion (score 2) per AGREE-II scoring principles. No clear description of intended users or usage instructions was found. The evidence does not specify target roles (e.g., 'nurses' or 'primary care physicians') but uses broad terms that could apply to any healthcare professional.
